newsitem.title: UK: S. Electric eyes long-term profitable growth.
newsitem.headline: S. Electric eyes long-term profitable growth.

text.p: Britain's last independent regional electricity company, Southern Electric Plc, said on Wednesday it should achieve long-term profitable earnings growth as it turned in annual profits within expectations.

Southern said pre-tax profits for the year ending March 31 were 255.5 million pounds ($417.1 million), compared with 283 million a year earlier, partly as a result of interest charges from its return of value to shareholders in January 1996. It paid out a dividend of 21.5 pence per share, up 14.7 percent on a year ago.

Southern, which had plans to link up with generator National Power blocked by the government over a year ago, said plans for two 45-megaWatt (mW), open-cycle, gas-fired power stations were well advanced with a further five sites identified for similar plants.

Investment in these sites should total 100 million pounds, Southern said, adding that it was investigating the possibility of expanding a 915-mW power station at Barking with a 125-mW open cycle gas turbine.
Southern said it looked forward "to the challenge of national competition in the domestic market...we are well placed for further growth as a leading national supplier".

Britain's domestic electricity market is scheduled to open up for competition from April 1998 but industry regulator Offer said last week that Southern still had "some way to go" but could be ready by then.
